title: Expose `pi.registerSetting` so an extension declares its own config key (Option B)
wave: 7 (settings ownership and the real unload seam: WI-8a, WI-8b, WI-9)
one_line: An extension can call `pi.registerSetting(definition)` at load time to declare a namespaced, typed, env-aware config key that behaves exactly like a core setting — visible and editable in the settings panel, reportable through the six provenance layers, and removable when the extension unloads.
user_visible_effect: A third-party extension ships its own settings: the key appears in the settings panel under the location M2-OQ4 picks, editing it writes to the normal settings layers (runtime/overlay/project/global), an env var can override it, and the panel shows which layer won. Two extensions that pick the same key produce a startup error that names the collision instead of one silently overwriting the other. Today the extension author has no way to do any of this — they write a side-channel file nobody reads.
effort: L. The public API surface is one method; the real work is the four blockers plus two the plan missed (owner-scoped unregistration and prepared-rebind idempotence, both verified below). Roughly: M for owner-scoped registry + invalidation, M for the loader/API/typing path, S–M for the panel placement once M2-OQ4 is decided (M if the panel becomes data-driven, S if extension keys land under the existing Plugins tab), S for tests. Do not start steps 5–7 before the M2-OQ4 decision lands — see open_questions.
risk: The dominant failure is silent and permanent, exactly as the plan says: expose `registerSetting` while the panel still cannot show the key, and the extension author gets no error, the user gets no UI, and nothing in CI goes red. The second failure is skipping namespacing — an extension id that collides with a core id throws inside that extension's own load, and the current message (`Setting "X" is registered twice`, registry.ts:787) names only the id, so the author never finds the real cause. The third, which the plan does not name: `register()` appends into module-level `byId`/`ordered` (registry.ts:778-779) that have NO unregister, so an extension that is disabled and re-enabled in one process will throw "registered twice" on its second enable, and `orderedSettings()` memoizes its result forever (all-settings.ts:85-89) so it will not even see a setting registered after its first call.
gate: Conjunction of two halves. (a) `bun run check:ts` — runnable today, verified green on HEAD; it goes red the moment `ExtensionAPI` declares `registerSetting` and `ConcreteExtensionAPI` does not implement it, because the class is declared `implements ExtensionAPI` (loader.ts:179). (b) `cd packages/coding-agent && bun test test/config/extension-registered-setting.test.ts` — BLOCKED in this environment until the native addon is built (`bun --cwd=packages/natives run build`); verified blocked on HEAD with `0 pass / 1 fail / 1 error` and `Failed to load pi_natives native addon for darwin-arm64`. All four test rows fail on HEAD by construction: row 1 and row 2 call `pi.registerSetting`, which does not exist, so the file does not even type-check. Rows 1, 2 and 4 are also runnable WITHOUT the extension loader at all (they go through `register`/`lookup`/`Setting.provenance` directly with a temp `Settings`), so once the addon is built they need no session, no TUI and no fixture on disk.
gate_can_fail: Yes, but state the split honestly. The type-check half genuinely fails: adding `registerSetting` to `ExtensionAPI` without implementing it on `ConcreteExtensionAPI` is a compile error, and a mismatched `SettingDefinition` return type is too. It will NOT catch the two things that actually break users — an unnamespaced id, and a registered key the panel never renders. Those are carried entirely by test rows 1, 3 and 4, and row 3 cannot be written until M2-OQ4 is answered. So the gate is real but it is not the whole gate, and the panel row is the only thing standing between this item and the plan's named "silent and permanent" failure.
verification: bun --cwd=packages/natives run build   # unblock bun test; verified: without it bun test reports 0 pass / 1 fail / 1 error
cd packages/coding-agent && bun test test/config/settings-registry.test.ts   # the 41 files of existing register({...}) call sites must not regress
test_contract: Four rows, all four required — §11.2 item 7 is not tickable if any is missing, and the plan is right that it is four and not two. (1) COLLISION IS SURFACED, NOT SWALLOWED: two extensions declaring the same setting id produce an entry in `LoadExtensionsResult.errors` whose text names both the colliding id and the fact that a namespaced id was required — not last-writer-wins, not a swallowed throw. Observable failure if it regresses: the second extension silently inherits or clobbers the first's key, and neither author ever learns their id was taken. Must assert via `loadExtensions`/`bindPreparedExtensions` (which collect into `errors`, loader.ts:497-505), NOT via `loadExtensionFromFactory` — the latter rethrows raw at loader.ts:473 and never produces an `errors` entry. (2) A REGISTERED SETTING IS A FIRST-CLASS SETTING, NOT A RENAMED STORE: after an extension declares a key, `lookup(id)` returns the handle, `handle.get(scope)` reads it, and `handle.provenance(scope)` names the winning layer across the five non-env layers — proving the dynamic key joined the same layer stack as a core key. Assert BOTH the resolved value AND the reported layer; a value-only assertion passes on a store that happens to read the right file. Assert through `Setting.provenance` (registry.ts:764-765), not `Settings.getProvenance` (settings.ts:800-808), which can never return "env". (3) PRESENT IN THE PANEL — BLOCKED ON M2-OQ4, see open_questions. After an extension registers a key at load, assert it is LISTED in the settings overlay at exactly the location M2-OQ4 selects, by building the list from the data source the panel actually renders. The verified data source is `createSettingsHost()` (settings-ui.ts:51-68), which iterates `SETTING_TABS` × `orderedSettings()` and keeps entries whose `ui?.tab === tab` (settings-ui.ts:53-56) — so the assertion is over `host.entries`, never over the DOM and never a source-grep of `settings-selector.ts`. (4) THE `env` LAYER IS OPT-IN AND OPTIONAL: a dynamic key that declares `definition.env` reports `"env"` from `provenance(scope)` when its environment variable is set, and reports a different layer when it is not; a dynamic key that does NOT declare `env` never reports `"env"` even with a same-named variable set. This row exists because `env` is per-setting opt-in — `#parseEnv` stays `undefined` when `definition.env` is absent (registry.ts:476-480), so `envValue()` returns `undefined` and provenance falls through — and because an overlay that merely re-renders the five old layers would pass rows 1 and 2 while silently losing env entirely. Assert the resolved value and the surfaced layer; never assert that "registerSetting was called".

steps.instruction: Confirm WI-8a has landed, and that its namespacing decision is written down. WI-8a is the hard dependency: `registerOwned` below refuses a bare id, and that refusal is meaningless if the substrate that owns extension keys does not exist. As of HEAD 808b365 `.lavish-wip/m2-specs/` holds only WI-0 through WI-7 — there is NO WI-8a spec yet, so WI-8b is being specified ahead of its own prerequisite. If you are picking this up first, write the WI-8a spec first; it is the shorter item (M, low risk) and it unblocks this one.

Add owner-scoped registration to the settings registry. Introduce `ownerById: Map<string, string>` and `idsByOwner: Map<string, Set<string>>` beside the existing module-level `byId`/`ordered` at :778-779. Move the body of `register` into a new `registerOwned(owner, definition)` and make `register` delegate to it with owner `"core"` — the signature must not change, because 41 files under `packages/coding-agent/src` call `register({...})` and all of them must keep compiling untouched. Replace the throw at :787 with a message that names BOTH the colliding id and the current owner, plus the namespace rule. This is the compatibility gate from GĐ6: no test asserts the old message (verified: `git grep -n "registered twice"` returns exactly one hit, the source line itself), so changing it breaks nothing, and it is the difference between an author who can debug a collision and one who cannot.

Add `ownedBy(owner)` and `unregisterOwned(owner)` next to `lookup`/`all`. `unregisterOwned` must remove the id from `byId`, from `ordered` (splice the matching handle out), and from both owner indexes, and must return the removed ids so the caller can invalidate derived caches. Keep it a no-op for an owner that registered nothing. This function does not exist today and its absence is the single most expensive omission available here: with append-only module state, disabling and re-enabling an extension in one process throws "already registered" on the second enable. `packages/coding-agent/src/config/model-registry.ts` is the precedent to copy the shape from — `clearSourceRegistrations(sourceId)` at :2914 and `syncExtensionSources(activeSourceIds)` at :2955 already do exactly this for providers.

Make `orderedSettings()` see dynamically registered settings. Two separate defects, fix both. (a) The `ordered` memo at :85-89 is never invalidated, so a setting registered after the first call is invisible forever — add `invalidateOrderedSettings()` and call it from wherever keys are added or removed. (b) `domainHandles` only ever visits values reachable from the 33 static `DOMAINS` entries at :43-77, so an extension-owned handle is in `all()` but in no domain and is silently dropped. Append handles from `all()` that no domain claimed, in registration order, after the static sequence. Keep the existing `sequence`/`seen` bookkeeping intact — it is what gives declaration order within a domain, and losing it reorders the whole panel. Where the appended block sits IS the M2-OQ4 decision; do not finalize it before step 6.

Widen the public API. Add `registerSetting<const D extends SettingDefinition>(definition: D): Setting<DefinitionValue<D>, D["id"]>` to `ExtensionAPI`, next to `registerFlag` at :1430, with a doc comment stating the namespace requirement, the collision throw, and the rebind-idempotence guarantee. Add `readonly settingIds: string[]` to `Extension` at :1802-1817 so the owning extension knows what it declared. Import `SettingDefinition`, `DefinitionValue` and `Setting` as top-level type imports from the config module — no inline `import("...").Type`, no `ReturnType<>`, no `any`. The interface currently has exactly 29 methods (verified by enumerating distinct leading-tab method names over 1256-1582); this makes it 30, so update any doc or count that asserts 29.

Do not write this step until the M2-OQ4 decision is recorded. Blockers 3 and 4 of the plan turn out to be ONE coupled problem, not two, and this is the correction that matters most: the panel's placement vocabulary is a closed union. `SettingTab` in `packages/tui/src/overlays/settings-defs.ts:4-15` is exactly ten literals; `TAB_GROUPS` at :52-88 is a static `Record<SettingTab, readonly string[]>`; and `createSettingsHost()` in `packages/coding-agent/src/config/settings-ui.ts:51-68` builds the panel by iterating `SETTING_TABS` and keeping entries whose `ui?.tab === tab` (:53-56). So an extension key can only ever land in one of the ten existing tabs — "a dynamic tab per extension" is not expressible without changing the union, and the existing `plugins` tab id is already outside it. Decide first, then implement: if extension keys go under the existing Plugins tab, also settle `:848-860` in `settings-selector.ts` (the schema-backed search, whose comment at :854 already says "Plugins hosts its own UI; it is not part of the schema-backed search") — fixing the tab list alone leaves a second surface where a load-registered key is permanently invisible, which is precisely what GĐ6 warns about.

Implement `registerSetting` on `ConcreteExtensionAPI`. The constructor at :191-208 walks the prototype and binds every method, so NO constructor wiring is needed — just add the method to the class. Model it on `registerComposerShape` at :277-289, which already validates its id and throws a typed error before mutating anything; that is the house pattern for "reject at registration, not later". Three behaviours the implementation must have: (a) reject a non-namespaced `id` with a message naming the required prefix; (b) treat a repeat call with the same definition by the SAME owner as a no-op returning the existing handle — `bindPreparedExtensions` (loader.ts:491-520) deliberately rebinds one prepared extension to a child session, re-running the factory, and that path is covered by the existing `test/extension-prepared-rebind.test.ts`; (c) push the id onto `extension.settingIds`.

Wire teardown. Add a `releaseExtensionSettings(owner)` helper next to the loader's other exported seams that calls `unregisterOwned` and then `invalidateOrderedSettings`, and call it from the unload path. WI-9 owns the general unload seam and its 11-bucket inventory; WI-8b's contribution is the bucket — the settings keys — and WI-9 must be able to see it or it cannot count it. Do not widen scope into WI-9's work here: land the helper, expose the ids, and let WI-9 sweep them.

Write the four contract rows described in `test_contract`. Setup pattern, copied from `test/extension-registered-tool-source-info.test.ts`: `new ExtensionRuntime()` + `new EventBus()` + `loadExtensionFromFactory(factory, "/project", events, runtime, name)`, imported from `../src/extensibility/extensions/loader`. For row 1 specifically, use `loadExtensions` or `bindPreparedExtensions` instead — those collect into `LoadExtensionsResult.errors` (loader.ts:497-505), whereas `loadExtensionFromFactory` rethrows at :473 and produces no error entry. For rows 1, 2 and 4 you do not need the loader at all: call `register`/`registerOwned`/`lookup` directly against a real `Settings` built on a temp dir, the way `test/config/settings-registry.test.ts` already does. `withEnv` for env mutation is already in that file — copy it rather than writing a second one. No `mock.module()`, ever.

Add one line under `## [Unreleased]` → `### Added`, user-facing, no root-cause narration: something like `Added pi.registerSetting so extensions can declare their own settings, editable in the settings panel`. If M2-OQ4 lands as a change to the panel's tab structure, that also needs its own user-facing line under `### Changed` — users who have muscle memory for a ten-tab panel will notice.

depends_on: WI-8a — hard prerequisite, not an improvement. The namespaced substrate must exist first: `registerOwned` refuses a bare id, and an extension key with no namespace collides with core ids through a plain string comparison at registry.ts:787. The plan is explicit that this is a precondition, and I confirm it: there is no owner, no namespace enforcement and no way to remove a key today.

M2-OQ4 — the panel-placement decision. Not a code dependency but a blocking one: steps 5-7 and test row 3 are not implementable until it is answered, and answering it after exposing the API is the plan's named silent-and-permanent failure.
blocks: WI-9 (real unload seam) — cannot complete its 11-bucket inventory unless extension-registered settings are an identifiable, removable bucket. WI-8b contributes the bucket; WI-9 sweeps it.
M2-OQ8 (per-extension state substrate, WI-11) — a decided answer here (overlay inside `Settings` vs a separate store) determines whether WI-11's state lands next to these keys or in a second store.
open_questions: M2-OQ4 — where does an extension key render? Three options in the plan (data-driven panel / under the existing Plugins tab / a dynamic tab). DECIDE, DO NOT DISCOVER IN CODE. Two verified constraints narrow it: `SettingTab` is a closed ten-literal union (settings-defs.ts:4-15) and `TAB_GROUPS` is a static record (:52-88), so "a dynamic tab per extension" requires changing both; and the existing Plugins tab is a PLUGIN (npm/marketplace) surface built from `plugin-settings.ts` with its own `PluginSettingsHost`, not an extension surface — putting extension keys there merges two different things under one tab. GĐ6 is right that this decision must also cover the schema-backed search at settings-selector.ts:848-860, not only the tab list at :431-440.

What makes a stable namespace slug for an extension? `Extension.path` is the path the user typed and is NOT stable — `omp --extension /abs/path` and a config entry spell it differently. `Extension.resolvedPath` (loader.ts:471, set from the absolute path) IS stable across rebinds and restarts, but embeds a machine-local path in a config key that persists in a shared settings file — bad for a checked-in project config. There is no manifest field on `Extension` (types.ts:1802-1817) to hang an author-declared id off, and no existing id-derivation helper (`git grep -n 'extensionId|slugExtension|normalizeExtensionId'` returns nothing). The marketplace has `buildPluginId(name, marketplace)` at `extensibility/plugins/marketplace/types.ts:29` as a shape precedent, but plugins get their id from a manifest and extensions do not. A human must pick: author-declared manifest id, resolved-path hash, or basename. Do not invent one.

Should the env variable for an extension key be author-chosen or derived? WI-8a settled this for plugins (`OMP_<PLUGIN_ID>_<KEY>`, uppercase, `-`/`.` → `_`, declared explicitly in `SettingDefinition.env`, never auto-generated) and verified the layer is opt-in at registry.ts:476-480. WI-8b should inherit that decision unchanged rather than re-derive it — but confirm WI-8a actually landed it as written before coding against it.

Should re-registering the same key by the same owner be a silent no-op or a throw? I specified no-op, because `bindPreparedExtensions` (loader.ts:491-520) rebinds one prepared extension to a child session and re-runs its factory, and that is a tested contract (`test/extension-prepared-rebind.test.ts`). But no-op silently masks a genuine double-declaration inside one extension. A human may prefer throw-on-second-declaration-in-one-bind with a separate rebind-detection path; the plan does not address this at all.

plan_corrections.claim: `config/registry.ts:783-792` is `register` with the duplicate-id throw; the only note on module state is the throw itself.
plan_corrections.correction: `register` is at :786 and the throw at :787 (the plan's :783 is a JSDoc line, :792 is the closing brace). The missed blocker: `byId` (:778) and `ordered` (:779) are module-level and APPEND-ONLY — there is no `unregister` anywhere in `packages/coding-agent/src/config/` (verified by grep). An extension that is disabled and re-enabled in one process therefore throws "registered twice" on its second enable, and its keys are unreachable for the process lifetime. WI-8b must add an owner-scoped unregister, and the precedent for the shape already exists in the same package: `clearSourceRegistrations(sourceId)` at `config/model-registry.ts:2914` and `syncExtensionSources(activeSourceIds)` at :2955 do exactly this for providers. This is also what makes WI-9's 11-bucket unload inventory tractable rather than impossible.
plan_corrections.evidence: `git grep -n 'unregister|delete byId|ordered.length|ordered.splice' -- packages/coding-agent/src/config/registry.ts` returns nothing. `awk 'NR>=779 && NR<=802' packages/coding-agent/src/config/registry.ts` shows `byId`/`ordered` declared once at module scope with only `register` appending. `awk 'NR>=2950 && NR<=2966' packages/coding-agent/src/config/model-registry.ts` shows the provider-owner precedent.

plan_corrections.claim: `orderedSettings()` lists settings by domain order then declaration order; a dynamic domain has no place in the panel (blocker 3).
plan_corrections.verdict: incomplete — there is a second, sharper failure the plan does not name
plan_corrections.correction: Two defects, not one. (a) `all-settings.ts:85-89` memoizes `ordered` in a module-level `let` with NO invalidation, so any setting registered after the first `orderedSettings()` call is invisible forever — regardless of panel placement. (b) `domainHandles` (:92-106) only ever walks values reachable from the 33 static `DOMAINS` entries, so an extension handle that IS in `registry.all()` is silently dropped. The plan describes (b) as "no place in the panel"; (a) is worse because it is order-dependent and would not show up in a test that happens to register before the first call.
plan_corrections.evidence: `awk 'NR>=78 && NR<=160' packages/coding-agent/src/config/all-settings.ts` shows `let ordered` at :85, `if (ordered) return ordered;` at :89, and `domainHandles` at :92-106 iterating only `for (const key in domain)`. No invalidation function exists anywhere in the file.

plan_corrections.claim: A test row asserting that a duplicate id produces an error surfaced to the extension author fails on HEAD because "the loader has no obligation to propagate it today".
plan_corrections.verdict: wrong in detail — the loader already propagates; what is missing is a message that names the collision
plan_corrections.correction: The loader DOES surface factory errors. `runExtensionFactory` (loader.ts:397-414) rethrows, `bindExtension` (:438-459) catches and returns `Failed to load extension: <message>` at :457, and `bindPreparedExtensions` (:491-520) collects those into `LoadExtensionsResult.errors` (:497-505), which `formatExtensionLoadNotifications` (`load-errors.ts`) renders to the user. So the propagation path exists and needs no work. The actual gap is that the current message is `Setting "X" is registered twice` — it names the id but not the owner and not the namespace rule, which is exactly the GĐ6 compatibility gate. The test-design consequence is concrete and easy to get wrong: assert the collision through `loadExtensions`/`bindPreparedExtensions` and read `result.errors`, NOT through `loadExtensionFromFactory` (:464-475), which rethrows at :473 and never populates `errors`.
plan_corrections.evidence: `awk 'NR>=380 && NR<=470' packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/loader.ts` shows all three functions. `cat packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/load-errors.ts` shows the formatter. `git grep -n 'bindPreparedExtensions|errors.push|errors:' -- .../loader.ts` → :497 and :505.

plan_corrections.claim: `pi.registerSetting` is added as the 30th method on `ExtensionAPI`, and the `ConcreteExtensionAPI` wiring follows the pattern of the existing registration methods.
plan_corrections.verdict: correct, with one saving worth knowing
plan_corrections.correction: Confirmed, and better than the plan assumes: NO wiring is needed. `ConcreteExtensionAPI`'s constructor (loader.ts:191-208) walks `ConcreteExtensionAPI.prototype` and rebinds every method onto the instance, and the comment at :198-200 says so explicitly ("Walk the prototype rather than listing methods: a new method is bound without touching this"). The class is declared `implements ExtensionAPI, IExtensionRuntime` (:179), so omitting the implementation is a compile error — which is what makes the `check:ts` half of the gate real rather than decorative. The best sibling template is not `registerFlag` (:259-267) but `registerComposerShape` (:277-289), which already validates its id and throws a typed error before mutating any state.
plan_corrections.evidence: `awk 'NR>=179 && NR<=290' packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/loader.ts` shows the prototype-walk constructor, `registerFlag`, and `registerComposerShape`'s validate-then-throw body. `bun run check:ts` passes on HEAD (all 15 packages report Done), confirming the current baseline is green.

plan_corrections.verdict: correct as written, but the second half is blocked in this environment — flag it before assigning
plan_corrections.correction: `bun run check:ts` runs and passes on HEAD 808b365 (verified: all 15 packages report Done). `bun test` does NOT: running an existing test in that directory reports `0 pass / 1 fail / 1 error` with `Failed to load pi_natives native addon for darwin-arm64` and points at `bun --cwd=packages/natives run build`. So the four test rows cannot be executed until the addon is built. This does not weaken the work — rows 1, 2 and 4 need no loader, no session and no fixture on disk — but the assignee must know the gate is half-runnable today, and should not read a `bun test` failure as a regression in their own change.
